name: Scan Docker Image for Vulnerabilities (management rendition)
description: Perform a Trivy-based security scan on a specified Docker image to identify high and critical vulnerabilities. Reported as a release decision.

reporting.expectedOutput: Release verdict, worst-severity findings, and the compliance headline, without the full issue list

notes: Sibling of sample_intent_image_scan_technical.json with the same target, parameters and criteria. This is the best example in the whole sample set of the max_findings cap: 25 canonical findings, 5 shown, 20 counted in reportProfile.findingsOmitted. A top-5 list that did not carry the omission count would read as the complete vulnerability set of the image; the count exists to prevent that misread. Findings reduce by selection (severity floor, top-N), not by aggregation. The management profile reports the verdict, the five highest-priority items, and the compliance headline, but not all 25 findings. Note that the 25 findings are in the base image's OS packages and Python dependencies — third-party components — which is why the obligations that resolve to assessed are the ones about detecting published vulnerabilities (ISO 27001 A.8.8, DORA Art. 10) rather than the supply-chain control itself: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) is the requirement about supplier relationships, and it is not among the criteria named here. Twenty-five findings in an unmodified official base image is a normal result, not an alarming one; it is what a public image looks like against a HIGH/CRITICAL filter.
